subject: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>, Michael Turner <michael.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure and success criteria

Hi Sofia

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 30 min discovery so we have aligned next steps and success criteria. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Unit economics are the primary blocker: per-message token costs are driving up CAC and making certain flows unprofitable.
- Spiky traffic with unpredictable peaks; current infra struggles to hit latency targets during spikes.
- Current stack is a mix of managed cloud endpoints + a small on-prem GPU fleet for sensitive workloads. You mentioned a desire to keep some inference local for latency/regulatory reasons.

Current stack / telemetry (what you told us):
- Primary model: open LLM tuned for dialogue, ~13B parameters (mixed 16-bit / 8-bit run on current infra).
- Avg QPS: 12 baseline, peak bursts up to 180 for short windows.
- Typical prompt length: 400-700 tokens; responses avg ~120 tokens.
- Current provider invoicing shows ~3.2x higher per-token cost than your internal target for production.

Success criteria you listed:
- Reduce per-request inference cost by >= 50% while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms for core flows.
- Predictable unit economics: ability to model $/1000 requests under different load shapes.
- Clear rollout path: pilot on a subset of traffic, then expand to 100% with fallbacks.

Technical assumptions / preferences you mentioned:
- Open to model quantization and 4-bit or 8-bit approaches if quality holds.
- Interested in both batching and KV/prefix caching as levers to reduce cost.
- Willing to try a dedicated serving pool (reserved capacity) if it gives predictable throughput and unit costs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team and our Solutions Engineering team 60 min to go over traffic shapes, sample prompts, and telemetry. Ben suggested Monday/Tuesday next week as options.
2) You to share recent telemetry exports (90 days preferred) and an example prompt set; we can run a quick cost simulation.
3) Redwood to deliver a short preliminary sizing & cost model (incl. batching/caching impact and quantization scenarios).

Attachments: we requested a sample telemetry export during the call please attach when convenient.

If that looks right I'll get Ben on the calendar for the deep-dive and put together the initial cost model.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Turner <michael.turner@finbot.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure and success criteria

Thanks Marissa this is great and accurate. We appreciate the clear next steps.

I've attached the telemetry export (90 days aggregated) and a short PDF with our recent SLA/latency targets. Key clarifications:
- Peaks are usually end-of-month statement generation windows (10-15 minute bursts).
- We absolutely need 95th pct latency < 300ms for customer-facing chat; background batch jobs can be slower.
- Quantization: our ML lead is cautious but open to 4-bit if we can A/B test quality on user prompts.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Mon Apr 26 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue Apr 27 14:00-15:00 PT. Ben, do either work for you?

Attachments:
- finbot-aggregate-telemetry-20270422.csv
- finbot-qps-sla.pdf

Best,
Sofia Ramos
VP Product | FinBot
sofia@finbot.ai
+1 (617) 555-0912

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>, Michael Turner <michael.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure and success criteria

Perfect thanks for the files, Sofia. We reviewed the telemetry and that pattern lines up with what we suspected.

Ben / Dev Monday 10:00 PT works on our side; I'll book the 60 min slot and include a short pre-read. Agenda for the deep-dive:
- Walkthrough of FinBot telemetry and critical prompt examples (10 min)
- Redwood latency/cost levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization options (25 min)
- Pilot plan & success metrics (15 min)
- Action items and timeline (10 min)

Pre-read requests for your infra/ML team: a) top 25 prompt examples & label for quality sensitivity (which prompts are high-risk for quantization), b) confirmation of which flows must stay on-prem vs allowed to be routed to hosted pools.

We will come prepared with an initial cost model (baseline vs with batching/caching vs quantized runs). For the pilot we recommend a conservative A/B on 10-20% of traffic to validate quality and latency before expanding.

I'll send a calendar invite for Mon Apr 26 10:00 PT and attach the pre-read template.

Thanks looking forward to it.

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure and success criteria

Hi Sofia appreciate you sending the telemetry. A few quick notes ahead of Monday: 

1) From the aggregate we can start with two concrete scenarios to model:
   - Batching + prefix caching enabled on hosted pools (simulate average QPS and burst smoothing)
   - Dedicated reserved capacity with offline quantization experiments (4-bit / 8-bit) to estimate quality tradeoffs and unit cost

2) What we'll bring on Monday:
   - A lightweight cost model (cost per 1k requests) for the two scenarios above
   - A simple benchmarking plan and sample scripts to run on your infra during the pilot (we'll keep it non-disruptive)
   - A QA checklist for quantization-sensitive prompts so we can prioritize which prompts to hold back from early quantized runs

3) Quick question for your ML lead: do you have any strict disallowed ops (e.g., certain tokenizers, custom operators) that would prevent standard 4-bit quantization paths? If so, please flag on the call or share ahead of time.

See you Monday I'll include the benchmarks doc in the invite.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
